answer: Reputation portability escrow: an agent’s earned rating lives in a shared ledger tied to its work history, and cloning a new identity starts it at zero. Each clone must climb the same verification trellis from scratch, paying the full time and fee cost of re-earning trust before it can transact at scale. Because honest agents carry their score across contexts, the attacker’s cost grows in a spiral with every duplicate, while a legitimate operator pays once. A dune of fresh identities buys no shortcut, only multiplied onboarding expense.
